title: API-driven batching & KV-cache recommendation executor with transactional apply and safe rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a production-ready API + webhook flow and SDK helpers to safely apply batching and KV-cache recommendations generated by Redwood Optimize. The flow must support idempotent apply operations, dry-run validation, observable status updates (via webhook + status endpoint), and a deterministic rollback path if an apply causes regressions or infra failures. This ticket covers API contract, server-side execution semantics, webhook events, SDK primitives (Python/TS), and operational runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/optimize/apply accepts an operation request with op_id and returns 202 with a status URL for long-running execution
Apply operations are idempotent: repeated requests with same op_id do not double-apply recommendations and return existing operation state
A dry-run mode validates changes (shape, permissions, quota checks) without mutating production and returns a deterministic plan and estimated cost delta
Webhook events are emitted for apply.requested, apply.started, apply.succeeded, apply.failed, apply.rolled_back with signatures for verification
Rollback can be triggered automatically by policy (failed health checks) or manually via POST /v1/optimize/apply/{op_id}/rollback and restores prior config atomically
All applies and rollbacks are audit-logged, linked to the operator (API key or user), and surfaced in Console with token-level cost deltas
SDKs expose a single high-level method executeOptimizeOp(op_id, mode) that implements idempotency and exponential backoff for transient failures
End-to-end integration test harness reproduces a cost-regression scenario and validates rollback correctness and metrics emission
implementation_plan: Design API contract and schema (request/response) and publish OpenAPI spec in repo
Implement server-side controller to enqueue apply tasks with op_id, owner, and dry_run flag
Extend existing job runner to execute recommendation sequence: validate -> dry-run -> plan -> apply -> post-apply health checks
Add persistent operation store with last_applied_state, attempt_count, status, and audit metadata
Implement idempotency checks using op_id + checksum of recommendation payload and return existing op record if present
Wire webhook emitter with signed HMAC payloads and retry semantics (exponential backoff, dead-letter queue)
Implement rollback orchestration that applies inverse deltas, runs pre/post checks, and marks operation as rolled_back
Add SDK wrappers (python/redwood_optimize, js/@redwood/optimize) that manage op_id, poll status endpoint, and verify webhooks
Add Console UI hooks: operation timeline, cost delta preview, and manual rollback button (frontend ticket will consume status API)
api_contract: POST /v1/optimize/apply  -- body: {op_id:string, recommendations:list, dry_run:bool, requester:string, idempotency_key?:string} => 202 {operation_url}
PATCH /v1/optimize/operations/{op_id} -- restricted for internal hooks to update operation state
webhook_spec: Events: optimize.apply.requested, optimize.apply.started, optimize.apply.succeeded, optimize.apply.failed, optimize.apply.rolled_back
Payload includes: op_id, timestamp, status, summary: {applied_changes, cost_delta_estimate, affected_routes}, requestor_id
Signature: X-Redwood-Signature header = HMAC_SHA256(payload, webhook_secret) - SDKs verify before acting
Retry: 5 attempts with exponential backoff; permanent failures go to DLQ and surface in Console
Delivery guaranteed semantics: webhook emitter records delivery attempts linked to operation in audit logs
rollback_strategy: Automated rollback triggers: failing post-apply health checks, elevated latency (over SLO) on affected routes, or customer metric regressions reported by Monitor rules
Manual rollback: operator can call POST /v1/optimize/operations/{op_id}/rollback or trigger from Console

Rollback steps: 1) compute inverse deltas from last_applied_state; 2) validate inverse against current infra; 3) apply inverse in same transactional runner; 4) run post-rollback health checks; 5) mark operation rolled_back and emit webhook
Safety: rollbacks are best-effort; rollback includes safeties (rate-limit changes, canary segments) to avoid cascading failures
Observability: every rollback must emit metrics: rollback_duration_ms, rollback_success, rollback_reason

2026-02-27 Liam: Implemented operation store schema and basic enqueue path. Left TODO: tie into KV-cache mutator and lock semantics for per-model routing configs.
2026-03-04 EngInfra: Verified job runner can perform 10 concurrent apply jobs in staging without OOM; observed occasional transient 429s from control-plane API - added retry with jitter.

2026-03-09 PM (Sofia Martinez): Requested UX signal for cost regret window (72 hours) and default automated rollback policy: fail-fast on >10% token-cost increase or >20% latency regression on canary routes.
